reports.extracted_text:
Patient Name: Karuna Chauhan | Age: 36 | Gender: Female
Clinical Vitals: BP: 130/90 mmHg, SpO2: 98%, Pulse: 82 bpm
Diagnosis / Clinical Impression: Anxiety with Gastric Discomfort / Dyspepsia
Rx Prescribed:
1. Pantoprazole 40mg (OD before breakfast)
2. Clonazepam 0.25mg / Escitalopram 5mg (HS at night)
3. Antacid suspension (as needed after meals)
Advice: Avoid spicy & oily foods, practice deep breathing exercises, review in 1 month.
reports.simplified_text: This clinical consultation notes symptoms related to anxiety accompanied by gastric distress (acidity and indigestion). Your blood pressure is 130/90 mmHg, which is slightly elevated, while your blood oxygen saturation (SpO2 98%) is very healthy. The doctor prescribed medications to soothe stomach acid and ease anxiety tension, and recommended mindful breathing and light meals.

entities.explanation: Blood pressure reading — slightly above optimal resting levels, often elevated during anxiety or physical discomfort.
Oxygen saturation — confirms strong and normal oxygen delivery in your bloodstream.
Indigestion or acid irritation in the stomach lining, often influenced by stress, irregular meals, or certain foods.
A medication that reduces stomach acid production to help calm gastric burning and promote lining recovery.

foods_to_eat: Oatmeal, barley, and bland warm porridge
Steamed zucchini, squash, and ripe bananas
Adequate room-temperature water throughout the day
foods_to_avoid: Heavily spiced, fried, or chili-laden dishes
High-caffeine espresso, energy drinks, and sodas
Heavy meals within 3 hours before sleep
recommended_exercise: Gentle walking for 20–30 minutes in the morning or early evening
Slow diaphragmatic breathing and relaxation stretches
recommendations.exercise_precautions: Avoid intense jumping or heavy abdominal strain right after meals.

reports.extracted_text:
Patient Name: Adhiya | Age: 20 Yrs | Gender: Male
Vitals: Temperature: 99°F, Blood Pressure: 115/66 mmHg, SpO2: 99%, Pulse Rate: 96 bpm
Clinical Impression: Acute Febrile Episode / Mild Upper Respiratory Infection
Prescription:
1. Paracetamol 650mg SOS for fever
2. Azithromycin 500mg (1 tablet daily for 3 days)
3. Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) in water daily
General Advice: Ample hydration, bed rest, review if temperature persists above 101°F.
reports.simplified_text: This prescription documents a mild low-grade fever (99°F) and a slightly elevated pulse rate (96 bpm), which is a normal immune response when fighting off an infection. Your blood pressure (115/66) and blood oxygen level (99%) are completely normal. The physician prescribed an antibiotic course, fever/pain relief, and fluid electrolytes for rapid recovery.

entities.explanation: Low-grade fever indicating your body's immune system is responding to a viral or bacterial challenge.
A widely used medication that lowers fever and eases bodily aches and discomfort.
Oral Rehydration Salts — replaces vital salts and electrolytes to prevent dehydration during fever.
High and optimal blood oxygen saturation, confirming your lungs are functioning well.

foods_to_eat: Clear vegetable broth, chicken soup, and warm herbal tea
Fresh tender coconut water and electrolyte rehydration drinks
Light soft rice, khichdi, or toast
foods_to_avoid: Ice-cold drinks and refrigerated desserts
Greasy, heavy, or ultra-processed fast food
recommended_exercise: Prioritize quiet bed rest and sleep to assist recovery
Avoid strenuous workouts or sports until fever-free for at least 48 hours
recommendations.exercise_precautions: Do not exercise while actively experiencing a fever.

reports.extracted_text:
Clinical Laboratory Report - Patient: John Doe (45/M)
Test: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c): 7.1 % (Reference: <5.7% Normal, 5.7-6.4% Prediabetes, >=6.5% Diabetes)
Fasting Blood Sugar: 126 mg/dL
Random Blood Sugar (RBS): 158 mg/dL
Serum Creatinine: 0.95 mg/dL (Normal: 0.7 - 1.3 mg/dL)
Impression: Elevated glycated hemoglobin consistent with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with sub-optimal glycemic control.
Medication: Metformin 500mg BID.
reports.simplified_text: This glycemic panel provides a 3-month average of your blood sugar levels. Your HbA1c result of 7.1% is slightly above the ideal target range, indicating your body is having trouble processing glucose efficiently. Your kidney function marker (Creatinine 0.95) is healthy and normal. Routine adherence to prescribed Metformin, balanced meals, and regular walking will help bring your glucose closer to goal.

entities.explanation: Reflects your average blood sugar over the last 2 to 3 months — slightly above standard targets.
A metabolic condition where the body does not properly manage circulating blood sugar.
A cornerstone medicine that assists cells in utilizing glucose and reduces excess sugar released by the liver.
A natural muscle byproduct filtered by the kidneys; normal levels indicate intact kidney clearance.

foods_to_eat: Non-starchy vegetables such as spinach, bell peppers, and cucumbers
High-fiber legumes, lentils, chickpeas, and beans
Whole grains like rolled oats, quinoa, and brown rice in modest portions
foods_to_avoid: Sweetened sodas, packaged juices, and energy drinks
Refined flour baked goods and sugary breakfast cereals
Excessive candy and dessert items
recommended_exercise: Brisk walking for 30 minutes 5 days a week
Gentle resistance band exercises twice weekly to enhance muscle glucose uptake
recommendations.exercise_precautions: Keep a small fast-acting snack on hand if taking walks far from home.

reports.extracted_text:
Cardiovascular Risk Screening - Patient: Jane Smith (38/F)
Total Cholesterol: 236 mg/dL (Desirable: <200)
LDL Cholesterol (Calculated): 148 mg/dL (Desirable: <100)
HDL Cholesterol: 52 mg/dL (Normal: >50)
Triglycerides: 168 mg/dL (Normal: <150)
Impression: Borderline hyperlipidemia with elevated LDL cholesterol. Recommended: Dietary modification, aerobic exercise, and clinical follow-up.
reports.simplified_text: Your lipid evaluation indicates that while your protective HDL ('good') cholesterol (52) is in a healthy range, your LDL ('bad') cholesterol is higher than recommended. Over time, high LDL can lead to gradual plaque accumulation in blood vessels. Boosting soluble fiber intake and choosing unsaturated healthy fats will help naturally lower LDL levels.

entities.explanation: Often called 'bad' cholesterol; high concentrations can gradually deposit along artery walls.
'Good' cholesterol that helps sweep away excess cholesterol from your bloodstream back to the liver.
A general term for higher-than-desirable levels of fats or cholesterol in the blood.

foods_to_eat: Steel-cut oats, barley, and foods rich in soluble fiber
Heart-healthy nuts like almonds and walnuts
Olive oil, avocado, and flaxseed as primary fat sources
foods_to_avoid: Trans fats found in packaged pastries and fried convenience snacks
Fatty cuts of processed meats and sausage
Excessive butter and whole-fat cream products
recommended_exercise: 30–45 minutes of moderate aerobic activity (e.g. brisk walking, cycling, or swimming) 4–5 days per week
recommendations.exercise_precautions: Begin each workout session with dynamic warming stretches.
